posts.caption: Dating apps weren't built for us. So we built one. 💗 Able To Love — where sharing how you move through the world is just part of your profile. You belong here. Join the waitlist → {{LINK}}

Dating apps weren't built for us. So we built one. 💗

Able To Love is dating where sharing how you move through the world is just... part of your profile. No third-date reveal. No over-explaining. No pity. Just people who get it.

You belong here. Waitlist link in bio.
1 in 4 adults lives with a disability. Zero mainstream dating apps were designed with us in mind. That math never made sense to us — so we're fixing it. → {{LINK}}
Every disabled dater knows THE moment. Do I put it in my bio? Wait for the date? Hope they noticed? On Able To Love, disclosure is optional, opt-in, and on YOUR terms. → {{LINK}}
The disclosure dread is real. We built the app that removes it. 💗 Swipe through — and join the waitlist via the link in bio.
"So, there's something I should tell you..." — the text no one on Able To Love ever has to draft. Your story is a green flag here. → {{LINK}}
Accessibility isn't a settings toggle on Able To Love. Screen-reader friendly, high contrast, big touch targets — it's the foundation, because it was built with the community, not for it. → {{LINK}}
We didn't add accessibility to a dating app. We built a dating app out of accessibility. There's a difference, and you can feel it the second you open Able To Love. → {{LINK}}
One week since we opened the waitlist. To everyone who signed up, shared, and sent us notes: you're why this exists. If you haven't joined yet — you belong here. → {{LINK}}
Green flags only: 🟢 asks instead of assumes 🟢 doesn't treat access needs like a burden 🟢 gets that a wheelchair is freedom, not confinement. What's on your list? → {{LINK}}
Real question for disabled daters: what's the ONE thing you wish dating apps understood? We're building Able To Love with your answers. 👇
Feature spotlight: on Able To Love, the "about my disability" section is optional and opt-in. Share everything, something, or nothing. You decide. That's the whole point. → {{LINK}}

Feature spotlight 🔍 Disclosure on YOUR terms.

Share everything, something, or nothing — it's optional, opt-in, and yours to control. Among people who already get it.

Waitlist link in bio. 💗
Chronic illness, neurodivergence, sensory, mobility — however you move through the world, you shouldn't have to write a cover letter to date. Able To Love gets it. → {{LINK}}
Waitlist members: check your email 👀 You can now move up the queue by inviting friends. Love is better with your people around. → {{LINK}}
Poll: what's the worst thing a dating app ever made you explain? Wrong answers also accepted. 😅
Two weeks in, and the waitlist keeps growing. Every signup is someone who's done over-explaining themselves to an algorithm. You belong here. → {{LINK}}

Accessible by design — a quick tour. 🧭

Screen-reader friendly. High contrast. Large touch targets. Built in from line one, because accessibility is the reason we exist, not a checkbox.

Waitlist in bio. 💗
How disclosure should feel: like mentioning you have a dog. How it feels on other apps: like a deposition. We chose the dog energy. 🐕 → {{LINK}}
To the adaptive sports crews, the advocacy orgs, the condition-specific group chats: we built this for your people. Come see. → {{LINK}}
"For the first time I didn't have to decide WHEN to bring it up. It was just there — and so was everyone else's." — beta member, on the disclosure field. This is why. → {{LINK}}
1 in 4 adults is disabled. The dating industry built for the other 3. We think the math is on our side. Press kit + waitlist → {{LINK}}
📅 It's official: we have a launch date. Waitlist members hear it first — check your inbox. Not on the list yet? Fix that → {{LINK}}
T-minus 7 days. One week until the doors open. Tell the group chat. 💗 → {{LINK}}
Meet the team: disabled people building the dating app we always wanted. Built with the community isn't our slogan, it's our org chart. → {{LINK}}
T-5. The best thing about launch week? Reading waitlist replies like "finally." Yeah. Finally. → {{LINK}}
T-4. Beta members have been matching for weeks. The stories are already better than anything we could write. Soon it's your turn. → {{LINK}}

What beta members are saying 💬 (shared with consent)

Swipe through. Four days to launch — waitlist in bio gets you in first. 💗
T-3. Ask us anything before launch: the disclosure field, safety and reporting, accessibility, the roadmap. We're in the replies all day. 👇
T-2. Waitlist members: your early-access email lands tomorrow night. Everyone else: there's still time → {{LINK}}
Tomorrow. 💗
The doors are open. Able To Love is LIVE. 💗 Dating where you belong — disclosure on your terms, accessibility by design, people who get it. Download now → {{LINK}}

WE'RE LIVE. 💗

Able To Love is officially here — dating where you belong. Disclosure on your terms. Accessibility by design. A community that gets it.

Download link in bio. Go find your people.
Launch day, evening check-in: signups are rolling, first matches are happening, and our team is grinning at their screens. Thank you. You belong here. → {{LINK}}
Day 2 energy: first matches are turning into first conversations. If you downloaded and haven't finished your profile — that's the fun part. Go. 💗 → {{LINK}}

24 hours in. First matches. First conversations. First "finally, an app that gets it." 💗

We're just getting started. Download link in bio.
What's next for Able To Love: more accessibility options, better matching, community features shaped by YOUR feedback. This app stays built with the community. → {{LINK}}
One month of Able To Love. 🥂 To everyone who joined, shared, matched, and believed: thank you. Know someone still doing the disclosure dance on other apps? Send them home → {{LINK}}
